memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water, and he will be unclean till evening. Any clothing or leather that has semen on it must be washed with water, and it will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now the chapter turns from illness to something entirely normal and healthy. And still: wash, and be unclean till evening.

This is where we must hold firmly to what "unclean" means. There is nothing sinful here. God designed this. Scripture celebrates marriage and the physical union within it — the Song of Songs is an entire book of unembarrassed love poetry, and Hebrews says marriage should be honoured by all, and the marriage bed kept pure (Heb 13:4).

So why the washing? Because this chapter is about the loss of what carries life. Semen, blood, the fluids that make life possible — when they leave the body, they picture life departing. And Israel's God is the living God. Everything associated with life ebbing away needed cleansing before approaching Him.

This was not a verdict on sexuality. It was a daily lesson in the holiness of the God who dwelt among them.

And notice the cost: a bath, and an evening. That is all. God made the ordinary rhythms of married life entirely workable within His law. He was not making His people ashamed of what He had designed.

God is not embarrassed by what He created. Neither should we be.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you absorbed shame about something God actually made good?
2. How does the difference between "unclean" and "sinful" change your reading?
3. What does it mean to honour God with your body in this area?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You made the human body and called it good. Free me from false shame, and help me honour You in every part of life, including this one. Amen.
